llm.summary: This skill is a coherent research-workflow CLI that uses local files, academic APIs, and user-directed scripts in ways that are disclosed and aligned with its purpose.

dimensions.detail: The skill needs local project file read/write and network calls to academic APIs for search/priority checks. It also runs user-selected certificate scripts, which is powerful but disclosed and central to the certificate feature.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is ordinary Python usage with optional requirements for PDF parsing/tests. Maintainer packaging/export scripts are present and documented, including Coze-specific export behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions are command documentation and integrity rules; I found no prompt hijacking, hidden role changes, or instructions to override user or system controls.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistence is limited to user-directed project artifacts such as JSON ledgers, session state, reports, manifests, and generated templates. I found no background service, startup hook, credential store access, or cross-session backdoor.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The advertised lifecycle is supported by shipped command dispatch and scripts for project setup, literature search, PDF analysis, LaTeX scaffolding, experiments, proof ledger, priority checks, certificates, revision tracking, and audits.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install if you are comfortable with a command-line research tool that writes into project directories, sends search terms/claims to academic APIs, and may execute certificate scripts you explicitly provide. Keep generated outputs in a project workspace and do not run certificate or packaging commands on untrusted code without reviewing it first.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The description-behavior mismatch finding is not supported by the full artifact: the broad command set is present and wired through run.py, rather than being only a single narrow script.
[AE1] unexpected: The referenced requirements.txt is present and contains optional, ordinary dependencies for PDF extraction and testing; I did not find analysis-evasion behavior in that reference.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese metadata is confined to the Coze export/listing path and is documented as platform-specific packaging, not a hidden runtime language restriction.
[LP3] expected: The skill does not provide a formal permissions manifest, but the needed file, network, and subprocess capabilities are described by command and are proportionate when granted only for user-invoked runs.
[AST4] expected: Subprocess use is mostly explicit-argument dispatch to bundled scripts or maintainer validation; the certificate runner executes a user-provided script, which users should treat as code execution.
[E1] expected: External requests go to documented academic search APIs and send the user's search or claim text; I found no credential collection or unrelated external transmission.
[A.I.G SARIF] expected: The supplied A.I.G scan reported no rule findings; my static review found no artifact-backed injection, persistence, or destructive behavior beyond documented maintainer and project-file operations.
